item.title: Ford issues a recall for 5,000 pickups over a wiring fault
item.description: Ford said the recall covers trucks built in January and February at one plant.
item.content:encoded:
Dealers will replace a harness clip at no cost to owners.

The company said no fires had been reported.

item.title: After restoration, the Tesla museum in Belgrade reopens
item.description: The museum holds the inventor's notebooks and a working replica of his coil.
item.content:encoded:
Letters between the inventor and Ford are shown in a new gallery from Friday.

Visitors can see the replica coil on the ground floor.

Our newsroom publishes corrections at the foot of every page.

item.title: Shell companies at the centre of a laundering case
item.description: Prosecutors said the laundering network moved 400 million euros through firms with no employees.
item.content:encoded:
The case names 40 entities registered in three jurisdictions.

Two banks have been fined for weak compliance controls.

item.title: Wall Street closes lower as investors weigh the rate path
item.description: The benchmark index closed 0.6 percent lower as investors weighed the outlook for interest rates.
item.content:encoded:
Trading volume was light and the session closed without a clear direction in either market.

Among the movers, $AAPL, $AMZN and $TSLA fell, while $V, $F and $TGT edged higher.

item.title: Shippers report normal service at the port
item.description: Freight forwarders said booking times are back to a two-day window.
item.content:encoded:
The port authority said in a statement that container traffic returned to normal levels within three weeks of the settlement.

It said the backlog of vessels waiting at anchor cleared on the ninth of the month.

A spokesperson said rail connections were the last part of the network to recover.

item.title: Software, energy and insurance lead the premarket movers
item.description: Analysts said margins held up better than feared across the sector as freight costs eased again.
item.content:encoded:
Among the movers, $ORCL, $SHEL and $GOOGL rose, while $META, $CAT and $ALL slipped.

item.title: Biz Daily | Pickup incentives are back in the market
item.description: Average incentives on full-size pickups reached 6 percent of sticker price last month.
item.content:encoded:
Dealers said Ford moved first with cash back on its most popular trims.

Analysts said Ford would defend share rather than margin this year.

One dealer said Ford inventory had climbed for a third month.

Buyers cross-shopping Ford took longer to close, the dealers said.

item.title: Insect numbers are rebounding, an Amazon basin survey finds
item.description: Ecologists said larvae counts in the basin rose for a second season after years of decline.
item.content:encoded:
Caterpillar species tracked by the survey recovered fastest in protected habitat.

Deforestation in the Amazon basin slowed 8 percent, the survey said.

Shell fragments of river molluscs were counted along the same riverbank.

Our newsroom publishes corrections at the foot of every page.

item.title: Biz Daily | Smartphone upgrade cycles are still lengthening
item.description: Two carriers said the average replacement cycle has passed four years in their largest markets.
item.content:encoded:
Carriers said Apple has stretched that cycle furthest, trimming quarterly sales of new handsets.

Analysts at two firms said Apple would offset the slowdown with services revenue.

One supplier said Apple accounted for a fifth of its shipments last year.

Rivals have not matched Apple on trade pricing, the carriers said.

item.title: Construction starts fell in January
item.description: Housing starts fell 3.1 percent in January while non-residential work held steady.
item.content:encoded:
Builders blamed financing costs rather than demand for the decline.

$CAT said in February that dealer orders remained firm.

item.title: Apple growers brace for a frost across the valley
item.description: Growers said an early frost damaged blossom across the valley and the harvest may fall by a fifth.
item.content:encoded:
Growers said Apple futures on the produce exchange rose 6 percent as buyers weighed a smaller crop.

Orchard owners have hired fewer seasonal workers than last year.

Caterpillar damage in the same orchards was lighter than last season.

Our newsroom publishes corrections at the foot of every page.

item.title: Debit routing rules reshape checkout
item.description: Processors said merchants now choose between two networks on most debit transactions.
item.content:encoded:
Processors said Visa keeps the larger share of routed volume in the market.

Merchants said Visa had matched rival pricing on small tickets.

One processor said Visa handles settlement faster on weekends.

Volume routed away from Visa grew 3 percent last quarter, processors said.

item.title: Regional bank raises deposit rates
item.description: The increase is the third since the summer and lifts the headline rate to 4.1 percent.
item.content:encoded:
The bank said in a statement that the new rate applies to balances above 5,000 dollars and takes effect on the first of the month.

It said branch staffing would not change, and that the decision followed a review of funding costs.

The chief financial officer said the move should protect the deposit base without hurting margin.

item.title: Visa settles interchange suit with a group of merchants
item.description: Visa Inc. (NYSE: V) agreed to cap interchange fees for five years under a settlement with a group of retail merchants.
item.content:encoded:
The agreement still needs court approval.

Cardholders will see no change at checkout, the payments network said.

item.title: Apple pie, but make it savoury: a recipe
item.description: The recipe swaps sugar for thyme and a sharp cheese, and it bakes in under an hour.
item.content:encoded:
Use firm apples so the slices keep their shape in the oven.

Bake the pastry Shell for ten minutes before filling.

A spoon of cider vinegar lifts the flavour.

item.title: A slow-burning thriller, anchored by Ford
item.description: The actor plays a retired pilot in a film that runs two hours and ten minutes.
item.content:encoded:
Critics praised the screenplay and the restrained pacing.

The film reunites him with the director of Oracle, a thriller from 2019.

Ford has not appeared in a cinema release since 2023, critics noted.

item.title: Alphabet cards return to the kindergarten classroom
item.description: Teachers said the cards help with phonics before pupils start spelling.
item.content:encoded:
The literacy programme runs for eight weeks.

The cards still start with A for Apple, the classroom teachers said.

Parents were given a short lesson plan to use at home.

item.title: Charging networks open up to rival vehicles
item.description: Three operators said cross-brand access will be available at most sites by the summer.
item.content:encoded:
Operators said Tesla had opened the largest share of its connectors so far.

Analysts said Tesla earns a margin on every session sold to other brands.

One operator said Tesla hardware needed only a firmware change.

Drivers using Tesla connectors pay a small premium, the operators said.

item.title: Ford Motor lifts full-year guidance on pickup demand
item.description: Ford Motor Company (NYSE: F) raised its full-year profit guidance, citing steady pickup demand and lower warranty costs.
item.content:encoded:
Shares rose 2 percent after the announcement.

The Dearborn assembly line will add a shift in June.

Dealers reported thinner inventory than a year earlier.
